## Install — no GitHub CLI, no tokens, no SSH keys

Download the **Source code (zip)** below, extract, and run the bundled installer. Same flow on every OS.

**macOS / Linux**
```bash
cd jtr-0.6.0
./install.sh
```

**Windows**
```powershell
cd .\jtr-0.6.0\
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1
```

The installer fetches `uv` if needed, then runs `uv tool install` on the extracted source. See [INSTALL.md](https://github.com/BD-AI-SDLC/jtr/blob/main/INSTALL.md) for manual steps and troubleshooting.

## What's new

`jtr auth sso` no longer downloads a browser. It drives the Edge or Chrome already installed on your machine, so the corporate proxy has nothing left to block — and the certificate workaround that existed to get around it is gone rather than simplified.

- **No more Chromium download.** The first `jtr auth sso` used to pull ~150 MB of Chromium, which Bosch's TLS-intercepting proxy blocks. jtr now launches your installed **Edge**, **Chrome** or **Chromium** over the DevTools protocol. Nothing is fetched at any point.
- **`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` is no longer needed.** Pointing Node at a corporate root CA only ever existed to get the download past the proxy. There is no download, so there is no workaround — the setting is gone from the docs and from the code.
- **Windows no longer needs WSL as a fallback.** The SSO flow uses the Edge that ships with Windows. `INSTALL.md` used to suggest retrying inside Ubuntu if cookie capture misbehaved; that advice is withdrawn.
- **Browser selection is explicit.** Edge is preferred, then Chrome, then Chromium. `JTR_BROWSER_CHANNEL=chrome` (or `msedge`, `chromium`) picks one; `JTR_BROWSER=<path>` points at an executable in a non-standard location. When none is found, the error lists every path that was tried.
- **Fixed: a saved cookie could vanish silently on re-login.** When seeding a fresh browser session from your saved cookies, Chrome discards a `SameSite=None` cookie that is not also `Secure` — with no error. Such cookies now keep their value and lose only the attribute.
- **Lighter install.** Dropping `playwright` (with `greenlet` and `pyee`) for `websocket-client` takes the installed environment from ~175 MB to ~40 MB, before counting the Chromium download that no longer happens.

## Removed

- **The bundled `/jtr-worca-bridge` Claude Code skill.** Its own compatibility check required `worca.sources.jira.hook`, which ships in no released `worca-cc`, so it refused to wire for anyone installing from a release. `/jtr` is unaffected and still installs with `jtr init`.

## Upgrading

Install as usual — your `.env`, PAT and saved cookies are all read as before, and no reconfiguration is needed. Two things to be aware of:

- **You need Edge, Chrome or Chromium installed** for `jtr auth sso`. Any Windows machine and virtually every developer machine already qualifies. Read and write commands don't touch a browser at all.
- **`/jtr-worca-bridge` is not removed from projects that already have it.** `jtr init` only ever copies skills in, so upgrading leaves any existing copy in place. To clean it up: `rm -rf .claude/skills/jtr-worca-bridge` in each project where you ran `jtr init`.

## Assets
- `install.sh` — macOS / Linux installer
- `install.ps1` — Windows installer
- `jtr-0.6.0-py3-none-any.whl`, `jtr-0.6.0.tar.gz` — build artifacts (auto-detected by the installers if placed alongside them)
